title: Word order 1: verb + object; place and time
subtitle: I like my job very much
summary: Learn where to put the object, the place and the time in an English sentence: verb + object, then place, then time.

lesson.heading: Verb + object stay together
lesson.text: The verb and its object normally go together. We do not usually put other words between them.

examples.wrong: I like very much my job

lesson.heading: Two more examples
lesson.text: Words like *also* and phrases like *on your left* must not come between the verb and its object either.

examples.text: I lost all my money and I **also lost my passport**.
At the end of this street you'll **see a supermarket on your left**.
examples.wrong: see on your left a supermarket

lesson.heading: Place (where?)
lesson.text: The verb and the place normally go together: **go home**, **live in a city**, **walk to work**. If the verb has an object, the order is **verb + object + place**.

examples.text: We took **the children to the zoo**.
examples.wrong: took to the zoo the children

lesson.heading: Time (when? / how often? / how long?)
lesson.text: Time normally goes **after** place, at the end of the sentence.

examples.text: They've lived in the same house **for a long time**.
You really shouldn't go to bed **so late**.
Sarah gave me a lift home **after the party**.

lesson.heading: Time at the beginning
lesson.text: Sometimes we put the time expression at the beginning of the sentence instead, especially to give it more importance.

examples.text: **After the party** Sarah gave me a lift home.

lesson.text: A simple order to remember: verb - object - where - when. Never split the verb from its object.

exercises.statement: Ben walks every morning to work.
exercises.explanation: Ben walks to work every morning. Place comes before time.
Correct. The object (German) comes straight after the verb, and quite well follows it.

exercises.statement: Joe doesn't like very much football.
exercises.explanation: Joe doesn't like football very much. Nothing goes between the verb and its object.
Have you seen Chris recently? The object comes before the time expression.

exercises.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order.
exercises.answer: I forgot to put a stamp on the envelope.
exercises.explanation: Verb + object (a stamp) + place (on the envelope).

exercises.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order.
exercises.answer: Did you learn a lot of things at school today?
exercises.explanation: Object, then place (at school), then time (today).

exercises.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order.
exercises.answer: Sarah takes her children to school every day.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has the correct word order?
options: I ate my breakfast quickly and went out.
I ate quickly my breakfast and went out.
I ate my quickly breakfast and went out.
exercises.explanation: The adverb quickly cannot come between the verb ate and its object my breakfast.

exercises.prompt: Put the parts in the correct order.
exercises.answer: My brother has been in Canada since April.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has the correct word order?
options: I didn't see you at the party on Saturday night.
I didn't see you on Saturday night at the party.
I didn't see at the party you on Saturday night.
exercises.explanation: Object (you), then place (at the party), then time (on Saturday night).
